subject: Request: temporary uptime threshold & credit adjustment
messages:
From: Sofia Delgado <sofia@helios-analytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Helios Analytics Legal <legal@helios-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime threshold & credit adjustment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles on the telemetry feed. We are close to finalizing the procurement approval but there are a couple of stickier items from our infra and legal teams related to the SLA.

TL;DR request: Helios is asking for a temporary relaxation of the standard 99.99% uptime floor to 99.95% for the first 6 months of the engagement, with a correspondingly reduced monthly credit cap while we run a data residency & load-profile validation.

Items they care about:
- Uptime floor: prefer 99.95% for months 1-6, revisiting at month 5 with agreed telemetry.
- Credit cap: would prefer a maximum monthly credit of 20% of fees (instead of the standard 100% full-month credit).
- Latency: p99 target of 500ms for inference; if p99 exceeds 1.5x target, they'd like a small credit band rather than a full SLA breach.

They also asked for a short runbook showing how outages are detected and how notification would work — attaching an example runbook they created internally. Can Redwood provide a worked example of the credit calculation for a hypothetical 2-hour incident at 95% uptime for a month? We need this detail for our budget committee.

If it helps, legal is OK with a timeboxed experiment provided the adjustments are explicit and there's an automatic reversion to standard terms after the pilot.

Thanks — looking to close this week if possible.

Sofia
Sofia Delgado
Head of Infrastructure, Helios Analytics

Attachment: runbook-availability.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Helios Analytics Legal <legal@helios-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime threshold & credit adjustment

Hi Sofia — really appreciate the clear ask and the runbook.

We can accommodate a timeboxed exception for the onboarding/pilot period with some guardrails. High-level proposal below (happy to sync live and then produce a short addendum to the Master Services Agreement):

Proposed pilot carveout (months 1–6):
- Uptime floor: 99.95% (measured per calendar month).
- Monthly credit cap: 20% of monthly invoice for any SLA-qualifying incidents during the pilot.
- Latency credit band: if observed p99 > 1.5x target for >6 total minutes in a 24-hour rolling window, apply a proportional credit up to 5% for that month tied to the magnitude of exceedance.
- Monitoring & verification: Redwood will provide per-route availability reports (daily) and a monthly verification packet with raw telemetry for the pilot months.
- Automatic reversion: Terms revert to our standard SLA (99.99% + standard credit schedule) at the end of month 6 unless both parties agree in writing to extend.

Example credit calc (requested): assume subscription fee $100,000/month and calendar month with 2.5 hours total unavailability that causes measured uptime of 99.65%:
- Baseline: uptime 99.65% < pilot floor 99.95% -> pilot credit applies.
- Credit calculation: proportionate credit relative to the deficit; under pilot cap, we'd apply 20% maximum. In the above scenario the raw proportional credit equates to ~20% of monthly invoice; since the cap is 20%, the customer would receive a 20% credit = $20,000.

Next steps: I can draft a 1-page SLA addendum reflecting the above and share for Helios legal review. If you want, loop in our finance lead (Ben Carter) and contracts (Laura Bennett) — cc'd here — so we can pre-clear the numbers and mechanics.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Termsheet_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime threshold & credit adjustment

Folks — quick internal sanity check before we send the addendum to Helios legal.

Ben: confirm finance is comfortable with a 20% monthly cap for a six-month pilot on a $100k ARR rec? If not, what guardrail do you need (e.g., minimum monthly commit or a partial prepayment)?
Marcus: any concerns operationally with providing daily per-route availability and the monthly telemetry packet? We should also confirm the measurement methodology and the single-source-of-truth time series we will use for disputes.

Two redlines from my side to include in the addendum:
- Explicit start date tied to first production traffic (so we don't start the 6 months during staging).
- A clause that requires both parties to sign the extension in writing by day 150 if they want to continue with modified terms.

Would propose we attach a short table in the addendum that spells out the credit tiers and an example calculation (Priyom's example is fine). Once Ben signs off I can shepherd the DocuSign and send to Helios legal.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Sofia — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short SLA addendum draft and a worked example table. Highlights:

- Pilot period: First production day through next 6 calendar months (we'll confirm the start date in DocuSign).
- Uptime floor during pilot: 99.95% monthly.
- Monthly credit mechanics: proportional credit up to a hard cap of 20% of monthly fees; we included an example table showing how the proportion is calculated and the cap enforcement.
- Latency: p99 credit band limited to 5% and only applies when p99 exceeds 1.5x target for >6 minutes in a rolling 24h window.
- Reporting: Redwood will provide daily per-route availability dashboards and a monthly telemetry packet (S3 link) for Helios to download.
- Reversion / extension: automatic reversion to standard SLA after 6 months unless both parties sign an extension by day 150.

Action items for Helios: please review the attached addendum and confirm the start date. Once you confirm, Laura will send via DocuSign and we can finalize the small-print with your legal team.

If it's helpful, Ben has confirmed finance is ok with the 20% pilot cap provided Helios signs a 3-month minimum billing commit during the pilot (Ben, please add if you'd like different language).

Looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
